ownership_reason: Only the gold reads the declarations of the enclosing local scopes and decides which of them a name refers to: hop 1 reads only the scope's own declarations (the facade's private map) and otherwise hands the enclosing scope on; hop 2 reads only the global scope, and only when the gold returns null; hops 3 and 4 pass the name and the scope along unchanged. Once the gold has walked past the nearest declaring local scope and returned the outermost one, no caller sees the inner declaration unless it repeats the gold's per-scope step itself or replaces the chain. The gold's javadoc promises the declaration that the name refers to from inside the scope; under JavaScript's lexical scoping that is the nearest enclosing declaration, which the variant does not return when two enclosing local scopes declare the name. The convention is pinned outside the gold: Scope.isDeclared (own declarations, then the parent's, returning at the first), SymbolTable.SymbolScope.getSlot (own symbol first, then the parent's) and LinkedFlowScope.getSlot (the first slot with the name, walking outwards) do the same step in production; ShadowVariablesTest testShadowSimple2 and testOptimal (a function's own declaration shadows an outer one), ScopedAliasesTest testShadowedVar (through the chain: an enclosing function's declaration shadows the global one) and TypeCheckTest testScoping1 pass.
